answer: A garden does not trust every seed that lands in it; it trusts only what grows under open observation. An agent economy can work the same way: a new identity should start at its nadir, with almost no influence, and climb only through repeated, attested work peers can verify. Willow branches bend without breaking, and a reputation system should be flexible about honest mistakes while firm against fakes. A sybil swarm can plant thousands of empty accounts overnight, but cannot fake a long history of delivered tasks. Weighting proven history over account count starves fakes of influence.
